questions.q: Why can't one task just read another task's local Python variable directly?
options: Tasks can run on different workers/machines, so there's no shared memory between them
Airflow technically forbids variables inside tasks
All tasks always run on the exact same process
Python doesn't support variables inside functions
questions.explain: Since tasks may execute on entirely different workers, there's no shared process memory — XCom exists specifically to bridge that gap.

questions.q: How does a @task-decorated function's return value get passed to another task?
options: It's automatically pushed to XCom, and calling one task's result as another's input pulls it automatically
It must always be written to a database manually first
It cannot be passed — TaskFlow functions can't return values
Only PythonOperator, never @task, supports passing data between tasks
questions.explain: TaskFlow's @task automatically wires XCom push/pull based on how you call the functions together — no explicit xcom_push/pull needed.

questions.q: What is the default XCom key a @task function's return value is stored under?
options: return_value
task_output
default_xcom
result_key
questions.explain: return_value is the default key used when a TaskFlow function's return value is automatically pushed to XCom.

questions.q: Why is passing a large DataFrame through XCom considered an anti-pattern?
options: XComs are stored in Airflow's metadata database, meant for small values — large data bloats it
Airflow physically cannot store more than 10 bytes in an XCom
It's actually the recommended approach for large data
XCom only works with string values, never structured data
questions.explain: XComs live in the metadata database, so pushing large data through them defeats the purpose and bloats that database — a reference should be passed instead.

questions.q: What's the recommended alternative to passing large data directly through XCom?
options: Pass a reference (a file path or table name) through XCom, and let the downstream task read the actual data itself
Increase the size limit on the metadata database
Store the data as a global Python variable
Avoid passing any information between tasks entirely
questions.explain: Passing a pointer to the data (like a file path or table name) keeps XCom lightweight while still letting downstream tasks access the real data.
